system.name: MAESTRO (Multi-Agent Environment Design Strategist for Open-Ended Learning)
system.one_liner: A regret-based curriculum for two-player zero-sum games that samples environment and co-player pairs from per-co-player buffers to train a student.

content.variant_note: a generator, a student, a co-player population and per-co-player buffers exchanging environments and regret through verb-labelled arrows, which together form a generate, evaluate, store, train cycle
content.argues: Co-players and environments should be curated jointly: regret measured per pair fills each co-player's buffer, and high-regret pairs train the student.
content.subject: The training loop of MAESTRO: environment generator, student agent, co-player population and their environment buffers.

lessons.what_to_learn: Give each member of a population one colour and carry it onto its own memory: a robot icon above a tile of the same colour holding a stack of sample thumbnails. Run verb-labelled arrows between population, generator and learner, and colour the keywords in the labels to tie them to the boxes they name.
lessons.suits: Population-based or curriculum methods (self-play, co-evolution, environment design) where each agent owns a buffer and a generate, evaluate, store, train cycle has to be read at a glance.

evidence: MAESTRO maintains a population of co-players, each having an individual buffer of high-regret environments.
MAESTRO continually provides high-regret environment/co-player pairs for training the student.

summary: MAESTRO is a multi-agent environment-design method for two-player zero-sum games: it keeps a population of co-players, each with its own buffer of high-regret environments, and trains a student on high-regret environment and co-player pairs. Figure 1 draws this as a cast of icons joined by verb-labelled arrows. A gear Environment Generator feeds a grey pair box, the Student Agent robot is evaluated against it, and the regret is written into that co-player's buffer. A dashed Co-Player Population of four coloured robots sits above four tiles of the same colours, each holding a stack of maze thumbnails; high-regret pairs go to a light blue box and train the student, and student copies are stored in the population.
summary_zh: MAESTRO 面向双人零和博弈做多智能体环境设计：维护一群协同玩家，每个有自己的高遗憾环境缓冲区，并用高遗憾的环境-玩家对训练学生。图 1 用齿轮、机器人、迷宫缩略图和带动词的箭头表示，同色机器人对应同色缓冲区。
notes: Prior labels kept (actor-interaction as multi-party-exchange, stage-pipeline read as a closed loop). The bottom framed region is treated as part of one drawing because it carries row labels, not a title, so panels is empty. The padlock's meaning on the store arrow is not stated in the figure. The reading of dashed versus solid arrows is mine. The coral student robot and the red co-player could be confused.
